result.summary: Fixes a crash in bitcoin-qt when run with -nosettings: three call sites in NodeImpl called ArgsManager::WriteSettingsFile unguarded, causing an abort on -resetguisettings and during legacy GUI settings migration. The PR guards those writes, skips migration when there's nowhere to migrate settings to (so legacy keys aren't silently dropped), and changes interfaces::Node::updateRwSetting to return whether the write reached disk. A second commit uses that return value to warn the user in the options dialog when a write fails, and to avoid requesting a restart that would discard an unsaved change.
result.problem: Users running bitcoin-qt with -nosettings (which the app itself suggests when the settings file can't be written) hit an abort in the options dialog and on legacy-settings migration, and the migration bug means stale legacy settings reappear on every start because the abort happens before the key removal that would otherwise fix it.

result.card: This PR fixes a crash in bitcoin-qt -nosettings mode: three unguarded calls to ArgsManager::WriteSettingsFile in NodeImpl abort the app on -resetguisettings and during legacy GUI settings migration, with the migration bug causing stale legacy settings to reappear on every start. It guards those writes, skips migration when there's nowhere to persist to, and changes interfaces::Node::updateRwSetting to report write success so the options dialog can warn on failure and avoid requesting a restart that would drop unsaved changes. The author found this while testing the related, already-merged #36176, which guards the fourth (wallet) call site to the same function. New Qt tests cover the disabled-settings and unwritable-settings paths, each of which fails without the corresponding fix. The PR has no reviews yet but appears ready to review, and the author notes the second (reporting) commit is optional and can be dropped if reviewers want to scope this to the crash fix alone. Not an IPC-infrastructure change despite touching interfaces/node.h; the interface signature change is incidental to a GUI/settings fix.
